name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_SEQUENCING_MCQ_Q01 - Developmental sequence of microsporogenesis to male gamete formation

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following stages and structures in the correct chronological sequence of microgametogenesis and pollen development within an angiosperm anther:

  1. Differentiation of potential pollen mother cells (PMCs) from homogenous cells
  2. Meiotic reduction division resulting in a cluster of four cells (microspore tetrad)
  3. Compactly arranged homogenous sporogenous tissue occupying the centre of the young microsporangium
  4. Dehydration and maturation of microspores dissociating into functional pollen grains
  5. Mitotic division of the generative cell yielding two functional male gametes

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the initial embryonic tissue in the microsporangium.
In a young anther, the centre of each microsporangium is initially occupied by a compact group of homogenous diploid cells known as the sporogenous tissue. Thus, stage III represents the starting point.

Step 2: Trace differentiation into pollen mother cells.
As the anther develops further, each diploid cell of the sporogenous tissue acts as a potential microspore mother cell or pollen mother cell (PMC). Thus, stage I follows stage III.

Step 3: Account for microsporogenesis.
Each pollen mother cell undergoes meiosis (microsporogenesis) to form a cluster of four haploid cells arranged as a microspore tetrad. Thus, stage II follows stage I.

Step 4: Trace pollen grain formation.
As the anther matures and dehydrates, the microspores dissociate from one another and develop specialized outer exine and inner intine walls to become independent pollen grains. Thus, stage IV follows stage II.

Step 5: Account for male gamete generation and conclude.
Finally, the generative cell of the pollen grain divides mitotically—either before shedding (at the 3-celled stage) or during pollen tube growth—to produce two non-motile male gametes. Thus, stage V represents the terminal step.
The correct chronological order of stages is: III → I → II → IV → V.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_SEXUAL_REPRODUCTION_IN_FLOWERING_PLANTS_SEQUENCING_MCQ_Q02 - Chronological sequence of pollen pistil interaction and fertilisation events

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following physiological and cellular events of pollen-pistil interaction and double fertilisation in their correct chronological sequence:

  1. Growth of the pollen tube through the intercellular spaces of the style towards the ovary
  2. Entry of the pollen tube into one of the synergids directed by the filiform apparatus
  3. Germination of a compatible pollen grain on the receptive stigma through a germ pore
  4. Discharge of two male gametes into the cytoplasm of the receptive synergid
  5. Simultaneous occurrences of syngamy and triple fusion within the embryo sac
  6. Entry of the pollen tube into the ovule through the micropylar aperture

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Initiation of germination following compatible recognition.
Upon successful chemical recognition and acceptance of a compatible pollen grain on the stigma, the pollen grain hydrates and germinates to produce a pollen tube through one of its germ pores. Thus, step III is the initial event.

Step 2: Traversal through stylar tissues.
The vegetative nucleus and generative contents enter the emerging tube, and the pollen tube grows chemotropically through the transmitting tissues of the stigma and style to reach the ovary. Thus, step I follows step III.

Step 3: Entry into the megasporangium (ovule).
After reaching the ovarian cavity, the pollen tube approaches the ovule and enters it through the micropyle. Thus, step VI follows step I.

Step 4: Penetration into the female gametophyte.
At the micropylar end of the embryo sac, special cellular thickenings called the filiform apparatus guide the entry of the pollen tube into the cytoplasm of one of the synergids. Thus, step II follows step VI.

Step 5: Discharge of male gametes.
The tip of the pollen tube ruptures within the penetrated synergid, releasing both male gametes into the synergid cytoplasm. Thus, step IV follows step II.

Step 6: Completion of double fertilisation.
One male gamete moves to the egg cell and fuses with its nucleus (syngamy), while the second male gamete moves to the central cell and fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion), completing the process of double fertilisation. Thus, step V is the concluding event.
The complete chronological sequence is: III → I → VI → II → IV → V.
